findings.title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup is not awaited
findings.body: getCalendar is now async, but the only call site wraps it in bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not wait for async callbacks, and the returned promises are discarded, so the try/catch around it never sees rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while external calendar events and video meetings may still be deleting, or may fail as unhandled rejections and leave the old event on the calendar.

findings.title: Wipe-my-cal reschedule cleanup is not awaited
findings.body: Same as the vital reschedule path: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) awaits getCalendar only inside a callback that nothing awaits. Calendar deleteEvent and video deleteMeeting are not part of the function's control flow, the surrounding try/catch cannot handle their failures, and the handler can finish (and email the user) before those integrations are actually torn down.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not wait for integration deletes
findings.body: requestReschedule now awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...), which does not await the callback. deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are dropped, so the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks without knowing whether the old calendar event or video meeting was removed. Failures become unhandled rejections instead of failing the mutation.

findings.title: Cancel-all recurring events never waits on calendar deletes
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking, credentials are walked with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) }). The callback is not awaited, and deletedEvent is the resolved value, not a promise, pushed only after deleteEvent finishes. Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) later in the handler therefore runs before those pushes, so recurring calendar events are not reliably deleted and errors are not surfaced to the cancel request. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly converted to for...of; this branch was not.

findings.title: Dynamic imports still load every app immediately
findings.body: Each app is stored as import("./...") in an object literal, so every promise starts as soon as this module is evaluated. Any importer of appStore (calendar, video, payment, bookings) therefore kicks off a load of every integration at once. That does not defer unused apps, and it replaces one static graph with many parallel chunks that all start together, which can make cold starts slower rather than lazy.
